battle.name: 牧野之戰
battle.brief: 公元前1046年正月，周武王率諸侯聯軍自周原東出，會盟於孟津，再度東征直抵商郊牧野，與商王帝辛的六師對壘。武王陣前誓師，左杖黃鉞右秉白旄，三軍同時壓上；商軍前陣倒戈，商軍崩潰，帝辛自焚，商朝覆亡。卡面月牙劍雖未隨軍而至，牧野陣上砍殺用的卻是青銅戈、矛與鉞。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 牧野之戰是商周兩方在今河南汲縣牧野的一次正面會戰。商一方是盤庚遷殷之後的商王朝，以商王帝辛居中，兵力為王畿的直屬軍隊與臨時徵發的方國之眾；後世文獻常把商的這支主力概括為「六師」，而《尚書·武成》只說帝辛「率其旅若林」。「旅」是商的軍旅編制單位，「若林」形容陣勢之密，並不是精確人數。商方掌握的還有王畿邑落提供的糧食、甲骨占卜所倚賴的龜甲與貞人集團，以及沿黃河北岸通往牧野一線的交通。助商的商族舊臣中，史載微子去之、箕子被囚、比干被殺，這些都是商廷內部裂痕的證據。周一方是文王受命之後經營了數十年的周方聯盟：周本身是陝西渭水上游渭原的核心，聯盟以受封建諸侯與被征服方國的首領組成，名義上奉周王為共主。《史記·周本紀》記武王在畢地祭天後「東觀兵至于盟津」，「諸侯不期而會盟津者八百諸侯」，這句話說明聯軍不是周方一支部隊，而是臨時聚合的諸侯聯盟。聯軍內部等級混雜：周人出的是自有的車兵與步兵，諸侯各出本部人馬；盟軍的糧秣大半就地徵發於周原與關中、豫北的周人據點，跨越大河之後只能靠取給當地。指揮系統極簡：最高決策在武王與師尚父姜尚，誓師、列陣與戰場決斷三事集於一身，各諸侯只負責本部作戰。牧野之戰因此不是一場王朝對王朝的全面戰爭，而是一次以聯盟形式進行的王朝更替。
countriesEn: The Battle of Muye was a set-piece clash in the open field at Muye, in what is now Jixian in Henan, between the two sides in the transfer of power from the Shang to the Zhou. On the Shang side stood the Shang dynasty as it had been reorganised since King Pan Geng's move of the capital to Yin, commanded in the person of the last Shang king, Di Xin, and fielded by the capital's own standing troops together with contingents hastily levied from the various subject polities. Later texts habitually summarise this central Shang force as the Six Divisions, while the Shujing's Wu Cheng offers only the phrase that Di Xin led his host like a forest; the word host is a unit of Shang military organisation, and like a forest describes the density of the ranks rather than any exact headcount. On the Shang side there were also the grain of the capital's settlements, the turtle plastrons and the divinatory corps on which Shang oracle practice depended, and the lines of communication along the north bank of the Yellow River down to Muye. Among the Shang's own courtiers the record names the defections and the punishments that show the dynasty cracking from within: the Prince Weizi departed, the Prince Zhi was imprisoned, the Prince Bi was killed. The Zhou side was an alliance built up over some fifty years since the mandate passed to King Wen: its core was the Zhou people of the Wei valley in Shaanxi, and around that core stood the feudal lords and the chiefs of polities that had been brought under Zhou control, all of them nominally recognising the Zhou king as overlord. The Shiji has it that after the king had sacrificed to Heaven at Bi he turned his army east and reviewed the troops as far as Mengjin, and that eight hundred feudal lords came to the assembly at Mengjin without being summoned, which says plainly that the force was not a standing Zhou army but a coalition hastily convened. Its composition was mixed: the Zhou contributed their own chariotry and foot, while each feudal lord brought such men as he had. Grain for the coalition was drawn largely on the spot from the Zhou base areas in the Guanzhong plain and in northern Henan, and once the army had crossed the great river it could live off the country it marched through. The command structure was simple to the point of being minimal: the highest decisions rested with King Wu and his military adviser Jiang Shang, and swearing the army in, deploying it and deciding the battle all fell to those two, while each feudal lord was responsible only for his own contingent in action. Muye was therefore not a war between two complete states but a dynastic change carried out in the form of a coalition campaign.
people: 這場戰爭留下姓名的，多數是勝方。周武王姬發，周文王姬昌之子，是聯軍的統帥；他在牧野陣前親自主持誓師與進攻，戰勝後入朝歌，其後數年即崩，年歲與卒年說法不一，《史記》只說他即位後數年而卒。師尚父姜尚，即後來封於齊的姜太公，是全軍的實際策劃者：出兵的時機、會盟的地點、列陣與渡河的安排都出自他手；他在《史記·齊太公世家》中被寫成「東海上人」，以渭水垂釣、願者上鉤的傳說聞名，而牧野的戰績使他成為後世兵家的祖師。《尚書·牧誓》把誓師之辭記在武王名下，其中「庸爾股肱」一類的話，正說明他召集的是諸侯之眾而非直屬部隊。姜尚之外的關鍵人物是文王姬昌：他在帝辛時代被囚於羑里，脫險之後回到周原，治周、擴張盟國、任用太公望，《論語·泰伯》所引「三分天下有其二」講的正是周人已掌握天下三分之二的勢力；今文《尚書》中《西伯戡黎》一篇，記的正是周人壯大之後商廷的憂慮。武王的弟弟周公旦在牧野之戰時隨軍，戰後攝政、平三監之亂、制禮作樂，是商周易革能夠落地的關鍵人物；召公奭則是另一支分封的柱石。商方留下姓名的只有商王帝辛本人，以及微子、箕子、比干這幾位反面人物：微子去之，箕子被囚，比干被殺，帝辛自焚於鹿臺。另有一類旁證：殷墟甲骨卜辭中「婦好」多次率兵征伐的記錄，說明商代王廷的女性可以正式領兵，這是商軍編制上值得注意的一個細節。
peopleEn: Few names survive from this war, and most of them belong to the winning side. King Wu of Zhou, Ji Fa, was the son of King Wen, Ji Chang, and he commanded the coalition: he personally conducted the swearing-in before the attack at Muye and led the advance, and after the victory he entered Zhaoge; he died a few years later, the years and dates of his death differing according to the source, the Shiji saying only that he died a few years after his accession. Jiang Shang, the Master Jiang, better known as Jiang Taigong and later enfeoffed in Qi, was the man who actually planned the campaign: the timing of the advance, the place of the assembly, the deployment and the crossing of the river were all his work. The Shiji in the biography of the House of Qi describes him as a man of the eastern sea and gives him the famous story of his fishing at the Wei, waiting for a fish that would bite; the victory at Muye made him the ancestor of the military writers of later ages. The Shujing's Mu Shi puts the words of the oath under King Wu's name, and phrases such as calling on the assembled lords to lend their limbs and sinews make it plain that he was convening a host of feudal lords rather than a standing army. The other key figure is King Wen, Ji Chang: he was imprisoned at Youli in the time of Di Xin, and after his release returned to the Zhou plain, ruled the Zhou, extended the alliance and employed Taigong Wang. The saying in the Lunyu at Taibo that the House of Zhou held two thirds of the world describes precisely the strength the Zhou had gathered. The chapter Xi Bo Kan Li, preserved in the received Shujing, records the anxiety of the Shang court once the Zhou had grown strong. King Wu's brother, the Duke of Zhou, Dan, marched with the army; his regency after the victory, his suppression of the revolt of the Three Supervisors, and his shaping of ritual and music were what made the change of dynasty a working institution rather than a slogan. Shao Gong Shi was the other pillar of the new enfeoffments. On the Shang side only the last king Di Xin is named, together with the counter-figures Weizi, Zhizhi and Bigan: Weizi departed, Zhizhi was imprisoned, Bigan was killed, and Di Xin burned himself at Lutai. One more piece of collateral evidence: the oracle bones from Yinxu record the Lady Fu Hao leading campaigns more than once, which shows that women of the Shang court could formally command troops, a notable detail of Shang military organisation.
kits: 先要說清楚一件容易被誤讀的事：卡面上的這把埃及月牙劍（khopesh），並沒有隨周軍出現在牧野。它是埃及自古王朝起就有的近身兵器，青銅質、單刃、刃口開在凸面，彎如新月，砍入人身或盾牌之後不必回抽；到第十八王朝，它在埃及步兵手裡已讓位給更省力的曲刃短刀。把它放進牧野的裝備表，是因為它屬於「青銅時代早期弧刃格殺」這一條技術路線的祖型，而牧野陣上真正砍殺的兵器，恰恰是同一條路線在東亞的另一個分支。西周聯軍的近身兵器以青銅戈為主：戈是裝在木柲上的斧刃刀，援部帶鋒、內部帶銎，砍殺時多用鉤啄與回拉的動作，與月牙劍「砍下去不用拔」的邏輯同源，只是柄更長、槓桿更長。與戈並列的是矛（青銅矛頭裝在木柲上）與鉞（斧形兵器，同時是統軍與賞罰的象徵，《史記·周本紀》記武王「左杖黃鉞，右秉白旄以麾」，那面黃鉞就是全軍號令的所在），以及商周式短刀。遠射兵器是竹木為身、以皮革加固的弓，配青銅、骨、石三種箭鏃，用於接戰前的壓制與兩翼騷擾。防護以木盾與皮革為主：商代墓葬出土的鎧甲極少，說明兩軍的重裝普遍止於皮甲與革胄，談不上成型的金屬甲胄。機動與衝撞靠車：殷墟出土的車馬坑顯示商代戰車為雙輪、單軸、軛轅結構，一車通常乘三人，兩人操縱、一人持戈或弓矛；周人把這套車兵技術用得比商更整齊，牧野正面衝鋒正是以革車先行。運輸與後勤靠牛車與人力搬運，沒有大型攻城器，也沒有投石機，因為牧野本來就是野戰：帝辛自焚的鹿臺是都城宮室的建築，攻城戰並未在牧野展開。
kitsEn: One thing has to be said first, because it is easy to misread: the Egyptian khopesh on the card did not march with the Zhou army to Muye. It was a close-combat weapon the Egyptians had used since the Old Kingdom: bronze, single-edged, with the edge on the convex side, curved like a new moon, and once it had been driven into a body or a shield it did not have to be pulled back out. By the Eighteenth Dynasty it had been displaced in Egyptian hands by a less effortful curved sword. It belongs in the equipment table of Muye because it is the ancestor type of one particular line of technique, the arc-bladed hack of the early Bronze Age, and the weapons that actually cut and slashed on the field at Muye were precisely a branch of that same line in East Asia. The close-combat weapon of the Zhou coalition was above all the bronze ge: a blade in the form of an axe head fitted to a wooden shaft, with a pointed upper blade and a socketed tang, used mainly to hook, to pull and to chop, which follows the same logic as the khopesh that one does not withdraw after striking, only with a longer haft and a longer lever. Alongside the ge stood the spear, a bronze head mounted on a wooden shaft, and the yue, the axe-shaped weapon that was at once a tool of war and an emblem of command and of reward and punishment. The Shiji in the annals of the House of Zhou records that King Wu took in his left hand the yellow yue and in his right the white banner of hair, that yellow axe being the token of command for the whole army. Short knives of Shang and Zhou type completed the list. The missile weapon was the bow, bamboo and wood with leather reinforcement, using arrowheads of bronze, bone and stone, employed to press the enemy before contact and to harry the flanks. Protection was wooden shields and leather: metal armour is very rarely found in Shang burials, which shows that heavy protection on both sides generally stopped at hide and leather, and there was no developed metal harness. Mobility and shock were the business of the chariot: the chariot pits at Yinxu show the Shang war chariot with two wheels on a single axle, a yoke and a pair of shafts, usually three men to a car, two of them driving and one holding a ge or a bow and spear. The Zhou used this chariot technology more neatly than the Shang did, and the frontal shock at Muye was made with the war chariot leading. Transport and supply rested on ox carts and human porters. There were no great siege engines and no stone-throwers, because Muye was a battle in the open field to begin with: the Lutai at which Di Xin burned himself was a palace building of the capital, and no siege was fought out at Muye.
tactics: 牧野的作戰流程可以拆成六步，每一步都留有文獻痕跡。第一步是祭與誓：《史記·周本紀》記武王「上祭于畢」，在周的畢地告天之後東出；《尚書·牧誓》保存了此行的誓辭，宣布此行是「恭行天罰」，並要求各部約束自己的士卒。第二步是「觀兵」與會盟：武王先率眾東至盟津（今河南孟津一帶的黃河渡口），「諸侯不期而會盟津者八百諸侯」；這是一次不打的閱兵兼政治檢查。通行說法是第一次會盟之後武王退兵，兩年後再出師（《史記·周本紀》記牧野之戰在武王即位之後第二年），既向商廷與諸侯表明並非非打不可，也等於測出聯盟的黏合度。第三步是渡河與集結：聯軍在孟津渡口分批渡過黃河，舟船輔以淺灘涉渡，先鋒車兵過河後在牧野一線展開，後方留人馬看守渡口與糧道。牧野在衛河（古清水）以北、朝歌以南數十里的平原地帶，聯軍深入之後糧秣只能就地徵發，因此不宜久戰。第四步是列陣：周軍以革車列於前，步兵居車後與兩翼，弓手壓在車前與陣邊策應；中軍是武王與姜尚所在，「左杖黃鉞，右秉白旄」以旗幟標定全軍的位置。商軍則在牧野南面展開，《尚書·武成》說帝辛「率其旅若林」，既說陣形密集，也說人多；商軍陣中除王畿主力外，還有大批臨時徵發的方國之眾與被徵役者。第五步是攻擊：出兵時間在拂曉，《尚書·武成》記「惟一月壬辰，旁死魄。越翼日癸巳」，「昧爽」是未完全天亮的時分，聯軍選擇在視線不清時發動，正是為了讓密集的商陣無法展開成有利的陣線。車兵先行衝擊，步兵隨之壓上，弓手在兩翼射擊騷擾。第六步是崩潰與追殺：史稱「前徒倒戈」，商軍前排掉轉方向，後排隨之瓦解，周軍趁勢掩殺，潰兵與倒戈者混雜在一起，《尚書·武成》以「血流漂杵」形容其慘烈，《孟子》則以「至仁伐至不仁，而何其血流漂杵也」提出疑問。牧野一役沒有攻城器械的使用記載，沒有圍城，勝負在一次野戰的正面碰撞裡決定。
tacticsEn: The course of the battle at Muye can be broken into six stages, and each leaves a trace in the sources. The first is sacrifice and oath. The Shiji in the annals of the House of Zhou records that King Wu sacrificed to Heaven on the way at Bi, and then set out east; the Shujing's Mu Shi preserves the words of the oath sworn on that march, proclaiming that the army was acting in obedience to Heaven's punishment, and requiring each unit to hold its men in order. The second stage is the review of troops and the assembly at the ford. King Wu first led the host east to Mengjin, a crossing of the Yellow River in what is now Mengjin county in Henan, and eight hundred feudal lords came to the assembly there without being summoned. This was a review of the troops that was also a political examination, and it was fought in no wise: a thousand years later the received account has it that the first assembly ended with the king withdrawing and that he marched again two years later, the Shiji placing the battle of Muye in the second year after his accession. The gesture told the Shang court and the feudal lords that the war was not a foregone conclusion, and it also tested how firmly the coalition would hold together. The third stage is the crossing and concentration. The coalition crossed the Yellow River in successive batches at the ford of Mengjin, boats assisted by fording through the shallows; the chariot vanguard came over first and deployed in a line at Muye, while troops were held back to guard the crossing and the supply road. Muye lies on the open plain north of the Wei river, the ancient Qingshui, some tens of li south of Zhaoge, and once the coalition had pushed that far inland its grain had to be taken from the country it occupied, which is why it could not afford a long campaign. The fourth stage is the deployment. The Zhou put their war chariots in front, the foot behind the chariots and on the flanks, and the archers in front of the chariots and on the edges of the line; the centre was the position of King Wu and Jiang Shang, with the yellow yue in the left hand and the white banner of hair in the right to fix the position of the whole army. The Shang deployed to the south of Muye; the Shujing's Wu Cheng says that Di Xin led his host like a forest, which speaks both of the density of the ranks and of the number of men, and among the Shang army there were, besides the capital's own troops, great numbers hastily levied from the subject polities and of men called up for service. The fifth stage is the attack. The blow was struck at daybreak: the Wu Cheng records that in the first month on the day juchen, at the time of the waning moon, and on the following day guisi the king reached the Shang suburb of Muye; the phrase in the dim light meant an hour before the light was full, and the coalition chose to strike while the sight was bad precisely so that the crowded Shang lines could not deploy into a favourable formation. The chariots charged first, the foot pressed on behind them, and the archers shot and harried from both flanks. The sixth stage is the collapse and the killing: the record calls it the front ranks turning their standards about, the front of the Shang line turning in its own direction and the rear breaking with it, and the Zhou pressing the advantage, the fugitives and the turners mixed together in the same press. The Wu Cheng describes the carnage with the phrase blood flowed and dragged the stakes, and the Mengzi raised the question of it in another register, asking why, if a most humane ruler had marched against a most inhumane one, the blood should flow and drag the stakes. There is no record at Muye of the use of siege engines or of any investment of a city; the outcome was settled in a single collision in the open field.
data: 可核對的數字分三類，來源可靠程度不同。第一類是文獻自述。年份：通行採用公元前1046年，此數由《尚書·武成》的干支（牧野在正月壬辰、癸巳）配合歷代曆法推算而得，此外還有1045、1044、1043、1041等說法，學界至今無定論。日期：《武成》記「惟一月壬辰，旁死魄。越翼日癸巳」，即農曆正月的朔日前後。聯軍規模：《史記·周本紀》「諸侯不期而會盟津者八百諸侯」，這是文獻數字；同一書說商軍「若林」，沒有可核的兵力。兵種與車數：《孟子》引述商末師制為「革車三百兩，虎賁三千」，加上誓辭中禁止士卒因追擊奔逃而擅離隊伍的規定，可見步兵是主體、車兵是骨幹。戰果：帝辛自焚（《史記·殷本紀》），周軍與商軍的具體傷亡數字不見於當時記載，只留下《武成》「血流漂杵」的文學形容。第二類是考古數字。殷墟自1928年起發掘，1936年小屯的YH127窖藏一次出土甲骨約一萬七千片，殷墟出土甲骨總數在十五萬片上下，已著錄者約九萬片，可辨甲骨文約四千五百字；甲骨卜辭裡保留大量征伐方國的記錄。婦好墓1976年發掘，出土器物一千九百餘件，其中青銅器四百六十八件、玉器七百五十五件；後母戊鼎重八百三十三公斤，是已知商代最重的青銅器。殷墟的年代距今約三千三百年，牧野之戰距今約三千零七十年。第三類是推估，必須打折扣：商末的人口與可徵兵員，學界分歧極大，常見說法是核心統治區在數十萬至百萬量級；牧野聯軍的實際作戰兵力，多數研究認為在數萬人上下，其中絕大多數是臨時徵發的步兵，職業車兵只佔其中一小部分。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into three classes, of very different reliability. The first class is what the texts say of themselves. The date: the year in general use is 1046 BC, a figure obtained by working out the sexagenary day recorded in the Shujing's Wu Cheng, the day renchen in the first month with the following day guisi, against the calendars of later times; other proposals are 1045, 1044, 1043 and 1041 BC, and scholars remain divided. The day: the Wu Cheng records that in the first month, on the day renchen at the time of the waning moon, and on the following day guisi, so the battle fell in the opening days of the first month of the lunar year. The size of the coalition: the Shiji has it that eight hundred feudal lords came to the assembly at Mengjin without being summoned, which is a figure taken from the text; the same book says the Shang host was like a forest and gives no verifiable strength. Arms and chariots: the Mengzi quotes the military system of the late Shang as three hundred war chariots and three thousand tiger warriors, and together with the oath's prohibition on the men leaving the ranks in pursuit of fugitives it shows that the foot was the body of the army and the chariot the skeleton. The result: Di Xin burned himself, as the Shiji in the annals of the House of Yin has it, while no figures for the losses of either side appear in the contemporary record, only the literary phrase of the Wu Cheng about blood flowing and dragging the stakes. The second class is archaeological. Yinxu has been excavated since 1928, and in 1936 the pit known as YH127 at Xiaotun gave up on the order of seventeen thousand oracle bones in a single deposit; the total from Yinxu stands at around one hundred and fifty thousand pieces, of which roughly ninety thousand have been published, and the number of legible oracle graph characters is about four thousand five hundred. The oracle texts preserve a large number of records of campaigns against subject polities. The tomb of Fu Hao, excavated in 1976, yielded more than nineteen hundred objects, of which four hundred and sixty-eight were bronze and seven hundred and fifty-five were jade; the Houmuwu ding weighs eight hundred and thirty-three kilograms and is the heaviest known Shang bronze vessel. The Yinxu phase lies about three thousand three hundred years back, and the battle of Muye about three thousand and seventy years back. The third class is estimate, and has to be discounted: estimates of the late Shang population and of the men available for levy vary enormously, the common view being a core controlled area in the hundreds of thousands to a million; the actual field strength at Muye is put by most studies in the tens of thousands, the great majority of them infantry hastily levied, with the professional chariotry no more than a small fraction.
cause: 打起來的原因有三層，層層相扣。表層是商王室的失政：帝辛在位末期用刑峻急、拒諫，殺比干、囚箕子、逐微子，弄得王族內部離心；卜辭中商王屢次為東方方國的叛離占問，說明商朝的軍事壓力同時來自東方，兵威分散，一支大軍壓在牧野一線並不容易。中間層是周方的崛起：文王姬昌在羑里之囚後回到周原，治周、擴張盟國、任用太公望，《論語·泰伯》所謂「三分天下有其二」講的正是周人已掌握天下三分之二的勢力；殷墟甲骨中也能找到商人把「周」當作必須占問的方國的痕跡，兩邊的關係從臣屬走向對峙。深層是「天命」這套話語：周人反覆宣稱商王失德、天命轉移，《尚書》一系文獻的措辭把改朝換代解釋為天的裁決，而不是單純的武力兼并；這種話語既給周人出兵找到了理由，也讓各路諸侯有了一面可以接受的旗號。技術層面的原因同樣實在：商的軍隊雖然龐大，編成卻鬆散，王畿主力之外是臨時徵發的方國之眾與被驅役的庶人，一旦統帥失了人心，前排的人掉頭就是最省力的破陣之法；而周的聯軍雖然雜，卻有共同的旗號、統一的時間表和一位掌控全局的軍師。牧野之戰因此常常被讀成一個警告：決定勝負的不是雙方的人數，而是商廷內部已經失去的信任。
causeEn: There are three layers of cause, each resting on the one below. The surface layer is the misgovernment of the Shang royal house. In the last years of his reign Di Xin was harsh in his punishments and refused remonstrance; he killed Bigan, imprisoned Zhizhi and sent Weizi away, and the royal clan came apart. In the oracle bones the Shang king repeatedly consulted the diviners about defection on the eastern side, which shows that the Shang military pressure came from more than one direction at once; with the war effort divided, it was not easy to hold a great army on the Muye line. The middle layer is the rise of the Zhou. After his imprisonment at Youli, King Wen Ji Chang returned to the Zhou plain, ruled the Zhou, extended the alliance and employed Taigong Wang; the saying in the Lunyu at Taibo that the House of Zhou held two thirds of the world describes the strength the Zhou had actually gathered. In the oracle bones of Yinxu one can also find traces of the Shang taking divination on Zhou as one of the polities that had to be dealt with, and the relation between the two houses moved from subject and ruler towards confrontation. The deepest layer is the discourse of the Mandate of Heaven. The Zhou repeated that the Shang king had lost his virtue and that Heaven had transferred its charge, and the wording of the Shujing documents explains a change of dynasty as the judgement of Heaven rather than as simple conquest by force. Such language gave the Zhou a reason for marching and gave the assembled lords a banner they could accept. The technical reasons are just as real. The Shang army was large but loosely organised: beyond the troops of the capital it consisted of contingents hastily levied from subject polities and of common people driven out to serve, and once the commander had lost the hearts of his men, the cheapest way to break a line was for its front rank to turn about. The Zhou coalition, mixed though it was, had a common banner, a single timetable and one strategist in control of the whole operation. The battle of Muye is for that reason often read as a warning: what decided it was not the numbers on either side but the trust the Shang court had already lost.
impact: 牧野之後，中國歷史進入一個新階段，這也是這場戰役在史學上位置特別重的原因。第一，商代成為信史。殷墟的甲骨文讓商王的世系、戰爭、祭祀與天象都有了可以核對的文字，牧野的勝者周人接手的，正是一個有成套文字與行政傳統的國家；有人說商周之際便是中國信史的起點，理由在此。第二，一套新的國家組織方式被建立起來。周公用禮樂、宗法與分封三件事把商朝的聯盟式結構接了過來，《論語·述而》所說「周監於二代，郁郁乎文哉」，講的正是周人對商制的改造；封周公於魯、封康叔於衛、封召公於燕、封姜尚於齊、微子封於宋（《史記·宋微子世家》），再往下分封晉、齊、魯、衛諸國，周王室的統治靠的是層層受封的關係網，而不是中央直接派兵。封建親親，以藩屏周，正是這套辦法的自我說明。第三，觀念上的後果最深：天命與德行的組合，成為此後兩千年改朝換代的合法性來源，孟子所說「取之而燕民悅之，則與之」，用的正是牧野這套邏輯；華夏與四方的區分、華夏族群的自我認同，也在這幾百年裡慢慢成形。第四，軍事上的教訓：一場野戰裡決定勝負的是「前徒倒戈」，是政治因素壓倒軍事因素；後世兵家反覆講「上兵伐謀」，講的仍是牧野的邏輯。第五，考古上的收穫：周原的西周甲骨與窖藏、曲阜的魯國故城、北京房山琉璃河的燕國早期遺存，以及岐山鳳雋村一帶出土的周初甲骨，把西周早中期的物質面貌一段段拼起來；牧野本身留下的痕跡則很有限，今河南新鄉衛輝一帶的牧野遺址經過調查與發掘，所獲多為西周早期遺存，學界至今難以把戰場位置完全定死。
impactEn: After Muye, Chinese history entered a new phase, and that is why this battle holds such a distinguished place in historiography. First, the Shang became part of the documentary record. The oracle bones of Yinxu gave the Shang royal lineage, its wars, its sacrifices and its observations of the sky a body of writing that could be checked, and the Zhou who won at Muye inherited a state that already possessed a full apparatus of writing and administration; some scholars date the beginning of China's documented history to the Shang-Zhou transition, and this is the reason. Second, a new organisation of the state was built. The Duke of Zhou took over the alliance-based structure of the Shang through three things, ritual and music, the patriarchal system and enfeoffment, and the remark in the Lunyu at Shueru that the Zhou looked back on the two former dynasties and how rich and civilised they were describes exactly the Zhou remaking of Shang institutions. The Duke of Zhou was enfeoffed in Lu, Kang Shu in Wei, Shao Gong in Yan, Jiang Shang in Qi and Weizi in Song, as the Shiji in the annals of the House of Song has it, and further enfeoffments followed in Jin, Qi, Lu and Wei. The rule of the Zhou kings rested on a web of reciprocal enfeoffments rather than on troops sent out from a centre, and the phrase about enfeoffing the kin to garrison and shield the Zhou is the system's own statement of its purpose. Third, the deepest of the consequences lay in ideas. The pairing of the Mandate of Heaven with moral virtue became the standard of legitimacy for every change of dynasty in the two millennia that followed, and the Mengzi's formula about taking the realm when the people of Yan are glad, and giving it to them then, works on precisely the logic of Muye. The distinction between Huaxia and the quarters, and the self-identification of the Huaxia group, took shape over those same centuries. Fourth, the military lesson: what decided a battle fought in the open field was the front ranks turning about, politics outweighing military factors, and the later military writers who spoke of the highest art of war being to attack the plans of the enemy were repeating the logic of Muye. Fifth, the archaeological returns: the Western Zhou oracle bones and hoards of the Zhou plain, the ruins of the Lu capital at Qufu, the early Yan remains at Liulihe in Fangshan near Beijing, and the early Zhou oracle bones from the Fengjuncun area of Qishan piece together the material face of the early and middle Western Zhou. Muye itself has left very little: the Muye site in Weihui, in the neighbourhood of Xinxiang in Henan, has been surveyed and partly excavated, yielding mostly early Western Zhou remains, and the position of the battlefield cannot yet be fixed with certainty.
result: 公元前1046年正月，牧野的會戰結束：商軍前陣倒戈，後陣隨之瓦解，周軍乘勢掩殺，帝辛回到朝歌後自焚於鹿臺（《史記·殷本紀》），商朝傳統所說六百年的統治到此為止；《尚書·武成》用「一戎衣，天下大定」四個字記這件事，同篇又說武王「乃反商政，政由舊」——先推翻商王，再收攏人心。《孟子》記武王誓師時說過一句話：「無畏！寧爾也，非敵百姓也」，既是安撫自己人，也說明這場戰爭在事後的敘述裡被定義為不以百姓為罪的戰役。有記載說武王入殷之後釋箕子之囚、封比干之墓、散鹿臺之財以振貧弱，後世講仁政講得更圓。戰後的收拾卻不那麼順利：武王其後數年而崩，成王年少，周公攝政，管叔、蔡叔、霍叔以「三監」之名叛（《尚書·大誥》《康誥》），周公東征平定，之後才有分封與禮樂的落實。結果可以這樣總結：牧野的勝利不是周人單方面打垮商朝，而是聯盟、倒戈與商廷內部失和三者合力的產物；它的歷史意義也不在戰術新穎，而在於它確立了此後幾百年的權力交接方式——以天命為旗號，以分封為骨架，以禮樂為形式，把一個王朝的崩解變成另一個王朝的開端。往後每一次王朝更替，人們都會想起牧野這個地名。
resultEn: In the first month of 1046 BC the meeting of arms at Muye was over: the front ranks of the Shang army turned about, the rear broke with them, the Zhou pressed the advantage, and Di Xin, back at Zhaoge, burned himself at Lutai, as the Shiji in the annals of the House of Yin records it, ending the rule of the Shang which tradition counted at six hundred years. The Shujing's Wu Cheng puts the matter in four words, one garment of war and all under heaven is settled, and the same chapter says that King Wu then reversed the Shang's government and followed the old way of things, overturning the king first and then gathering the people. The Mengzi has the king saying at the oath, Take courage; I am bearing you, and it is not the common people who are your enemy, which both heartened his own men and defined the war, in the telling that followed, as one not fought against the people. There is a record that after entering Yin the king released Zhizhi from prison, raised a mound at the tomb of Bigan, and scattered the treasure of Lutai to relieve the poor, though later ages tell the story of benevolence more neatly than that. The tidying-up afterwards was less smooth. The king died within a few years, King Cheng was a child, the Duke of Zhou took the regency, and the princes of Guan, Cai and Huo rebelled in the name of the Three Supervisors, as the Da Gao and Kang Gao of the Shujing have it; the Duke marched east and put it down, and only then were the enfeoffments and the ritual of the Zhou properly put in place. The result can be summed up this way. The victory at Muye was not the Zhou defeating the Shang single-handed; it was the product of the coalition, of the turners, and of the breakdown of trust inside the Shang court. Its historical significance does not lie in any tactical novelty either, but in the fact that it settled, for the centuries that followed, the manner in which power changed hands: the Mandate of Heaven for the banner, enfeoffment for the framework, ritual and music for the form, so that the dissolution of one dynasty became the beginning of another. Every later change of dynasty has called the place to mind.
